head: 4c3ba41f4c002d7416b688a81d8c48c424a82ec6
classification_reasons: Spec is tight after the panel: both of spec.md's Flagged concerns bullets literally begin with 'decided (by panel): ...' and their text matches decisions-b.json's 'item' field verbatim (empty input: ValueError('mean() requires at least one value') from a guard clause mean owns; parameter type: Sequence[float]), so the panel/cli.py ledger match the delegation prompt describes can succeed, and plan.md states one concrete signature and body rather than a range of options.

Blast radius is small: the diff (git diff <merge-base>...HEAD) touches only changes/0002-add-mean-helper-to-sample-pkg/{spec.md,plan.md,status.yaml,evidence/**}; no sample_pkg/*.py, tests/*.py, .claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md or sdlc.yaml is touched, and none of sdlc.yaml's risk_list items (auth, data migrations, money movement, production config) applies.

Coverage is the criterion that keeps this non-routine: mean is a brand-new function with no existing test exercising it; the three tests that will cover it (test_mean, test_mean_single_element, test_mean_empty) are written in this same change (phase c), not pre-existing. All three routine conditions (tight spec, small blast radius, code already covered by existing tests) must hold for routine, and this one does not.
attempted: Intent: re-read intent.md's Proposed outcome bullet 5 (spec closes flagged concerns as 'decided (by panel): ...', evidence/ carries decisions-b.md and panel/ files) against the current spec.md and evidence/ at this HEAD. Both Flagged concerns bullets carry the 'decided (by panel): ...' prefix, decisions-b.json/.md and evidence/panel/b-1-*, b-2-*, b-items.json all exist and agree with spec.md's literal bullet text and with plan.md's concrete decisions. intent.md's purpose for this change (exercising the deferred-review panel) is met.

Spec and plan: compared the exact text the delegation prompt describes: decisions-b.json item 1's 'item' field ('Empty-sequence behaviour for `mean` is undecided: `ZeroDivisionError` (via `divide`),') is a verbatim substring of spec.md's current Flagged concern bullet 1, and item 2's 'item' field is a verbatim substring of bullet 2 (after its duplicated 'decided (by panel): decided (by panel):' prefix, which sits before the item text rather than inside it). Confirmed spec.md was not touched by the tidy commit's revert beyond restoring this exact wording (git history: 3eeae7e edited it, 4c3ba41 reverted that edit) and that plan.md (untouched by the revert, per the delegation prompt and confirmed by its content matching what a prior 'panel decisions' commit would have produced) still carries the panel's final concrete decisions (Sequence[float], explicit ValueError guard) consistently in its Order of work, Risks and Options-not-taken sections.

Found and judged non-blocking: spec.md's Requirements bullet 3, the Design section's two paragraphs on parameter type and empty input, and the Open questions from intent section still read 'are not decided by this spec pass', 'This is not settled here (Flagged concerns)' and similar present-tense 'still open' language, which is now stale next to the Flagged concerns section's 'decided (by panel)' bullets a few lines below — an internal inconsistency in spec.md's prose (not introduced or removed by this HEAD's revert; it predates the panel round and was already present, and already reviewed, at HEAD 3514ccf). Per REVIEW.md's 'What Important means here' (reserved for findings that would break behavior, leak data or breach a policy; style and naming are nits) this is a nit: plan.md — the document an implementer actually builds from — is unambiguous and fully consistent with the panel's decisions, so the stale spec.md prose does not change what gets built, tested or shipped.

Proof: this is a design-only phase (b); no build/test/lint logs are expected or present, consistent with plan.md putting all code and tests in phase (c). evidence/panel/b-items.json shows decided: 2, pending: [], items: [], iterations.used: 2 of cap 2, gate: wait — consistent with status.yaml's iterations: 2 and with sdlc.yaml's gate.max_iterations_non_routine: 2 (both concerns closed, no iterations left, no overrun). decisions-b.json/.md and evidence/panel/b-1-*, b-2-* (reviewer, devil's advocate, conciliator) are internally consistent with each other and with plan.md's Options-not-taken attributions.

Blast radius: read sdlc.yaml directly; risk_list (auth, data migrations, money movement, production config), protected_paths and the always-protected guardrail files (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml) are all untouched by this diff. status.yaml's own review_override: deferred field is unchanged by this diff (only phase, iterations and updated_at moved).

Policies: re-read spec.md's per-skill applicability calls (security-baseline, ux-conventions, data-conventions correctly n/a for a pure in-process arithmetic helper) and the coding-standards rules (rule 2 match-surrounding-code, rule 5 no unnecessary dependency, rule 8 type hints/line length) the panel leaned on in b-1-reviewer.md/b-2-reviewer.md and the conciliator jsons; reasoning is specific to this codebase (divide/percent precedent), matches what spec.md and plan.md state.

Tests: no test files are touched in this phase-(b) diff, consistent with design-only scope; plan.md pins test_mean_empty to pytest.raises(ValueError) around mean([]), which pins mean's own guard clause rather than a coincidental ZeroDivisionError from divide — directly addressing the devil's advocate's point in b-1-advocate.md that a bare ZeroDivisionError-via-divide implementation could pass a weaker test with the wrong behaviour.
